utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Lukic, the Chamber was informed that you wanted to deal with a few matters, I think, remaining from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, we spoke with Mr. Weber in regard of D1261 MFI; and as I understood him, the Prosecution does not have objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Defence is correct, the Prosecution reviewed the whole video which is a total time of 6 minutes, 57 seconds, and we do not object to the admission of that whole video into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1261 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next topic is figures 70 and 71 from the report on Markale, which is 1D05496. You inquired about the source. Figure 75 was exhibit in Slobodan Milosevic trial, P636.1, and it was the third picture in that exhibit and it was found on the site of this Tribunal. Our experts found that on the site of the Tribunal. And...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's P636.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it was introduced through the witness Berko Zecevic. Figure 70 was the second picture in the same document, and 75 we also saw in the video, 1D05916.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not clear on the reference because I think there was two figures referred to but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First I addressed figure 75. Now I'm addressing figure 70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you started by staying the next topic is figures 70 and 71.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how it is on the record. Did you intend to say that your next topic was figures 70 and 75, and that you have dealt with 75 until now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and that you'll now deal with number 70?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 70, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it's -- so the second picture in the same P636 from Milosevic trial, and we uploaded it under our number as 1D05574.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then I take it, Mr. Weber, that you'll check -- because there was a difference in quality. I think had you a better quality. How it is possible that the better-quality version is found on the Internet --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honour. No. Video was brought by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, the video was brought by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, and it was given to Prosecution, and the Prosecution gave it to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I will, of course, check what the ERNs are associated to these exhibits and, if necessary, further inform the Chamber once we find out. The images that were tendered as part of this or videos -- well, I can check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would check that. Mr. Lukic has given you the clues to where it came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are tendering images and also yesterday, since there was discussion in regard 1D05916, we tendered it but it was not admitted. So I would use the opportunity to tender this video, 1D05916.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We have no objection to it. As far as we're concerned, it would be just -- it depicts what's already in evidence so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But better quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I -- I think the Chamber is able to assess the visual quality of the videos.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the Prosecution version, it's almost not possible to see those stones that were supporting the tail-fin -- it was very [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- the quality was different apparently -- I mean, the quality was not exactly the same as what we saw before. The Prosecution, if there's any concerns about differences between the two, we'll hear from them. Mr. Weber, you'll verify that, and you have no objections against 1D05916 to be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It still would be appreciated if counsel could give us the ERN associated to that, just so we know what the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We do not have ERN and we cannot give ERN. It's the Prosecution job, so we cannot give them ERN.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the concern is that -- I mean, to track it back to the source material and whether anything that happened to the video after that point in time, I need to know what the source material is and what that ERN is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I have answer to that. That video was brought to this Tribunal and given to the Prosecution by their witness Sead Besic during Karadzic trial, so it's easy to track.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And checking our records, that's the video we've tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which was P864.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But apparently you say, Mr. Lukic, it's different quality so something must have happened with that original material, either the Prosecution -- I don't know what has happened, but if the quality is different then something has happened with it. And what Mr. Weber would like to check whether what happened with the video, to know what was the original, so that can you see weather there was any manipulation or whatever by whomever; and for that purpose, Mr. Weber wants to know what is the source material. And you've now told him that the video that was given by Mr. Besic to the Prosecution, that it's that video -- but that's apparently the bad quality, so what then explains where the better quality comes from? And that's the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The better quality comes from the witness Sead Besic, who brought it here in December 2012.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the Prosecution tells us that that what is was tendered --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's -- I say that's what the Prosecution tells us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now then, of course, the question arises: You apparently have a copy of better quality --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They have it too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we may -- and if that's the case, all I'll need to know is just what the ERN is and I'll -- I would be -- before -- I'm happy to do whatever efforts are needed to resolve the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I would -- we are not going to spend time at this moment any further, but this little puzzle should be resolved before we finally decide on admission of the other version with the stones better visible. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could just take a care of couple other housekeeping matters. Going back to the Livanjska Street incident and discussion from Monday. This is the matter that relates to the 8th of November, 1994. The parties indicated that we would discuss the materials related to this event and their admission. I did have the opportunity to discusses with it with Mr. Lukic. There are three outstanding 65 ter numbers that have not yet been admitted related to these shellings. For the first shelling at 1525 hours under 65 ter 33104, which is the BiH MUP investigative file; and 65 ter 33235, which is the photo file. Those two items have not been admitted. And with respect to the second shelling at 1725 hours, 65 ter 18645 has not been admitted, which is the photo file. I believe it was the understanding that these would be acceptable to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Weber and I have to sit anyways and to discuss the exhibits that would come through this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. On my list is now 65 ter 33104 to be discussed; 33235, photo file; and for the later shelling another photo file, 18645, and we'd like to hear from the parties whether that is what the parties are seeking to have admitted into evidence. We then leave it to that for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'm sorry for interrupting you. I see that are you discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but it's finished, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid -- I don't like to have this video we received from the Prosecution in a limbo and to be on the mercy of the Prosecution to provide an ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We didn't say that. I think we -- what we said is the puzzle has to be resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But we cannot resolve it, so we are in the hands of the Prosecution. We cannot allow them to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we -- Mr. Weber will certainly sit together with you and then you -- you say you have that video and you have an explanation as to why you claim they have that video. Mr. Weber will carefully listen to that. Mr. Weber will check his sources, and then you agree or you do not agree. If you agree, there seems to be no major problem; if you do not agree, then you come back to the Chamber. You're not at the mercy of the Prosecution. You never have been and this Chamber will avoid that you ever will be. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want it on the record that we've disclosed everything with ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then -- okay, then fine. Then we have a puzzle that we should --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why would I hide ERN number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. -- Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- I don't understand the Prosecution objection, Your Honour. Why would I hide it? I'm interested to have this video admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic, if the Prosecution says they have disclosed everything with ERN numbers, then they have their records of disclosure and you have your records of what you received in disclosure. So apparently it slipped through; that's your position. Then you should explain when and how you got without an ERN number, whereas Mr. Weber's records say they have an ERN number. Try to resolve it, see where you can reconstruct how one or two versions were disclosed; and then if you don't agree, come back to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We leave it to that for the time being. One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I expect that the parties will have finished their discussions by next Monday, so if there's any matter not resolved by then, we'll further hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only we would like the position of the Prosecution whether their position is that something was tampered on this video by the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this -- Mr. -- that's a next step. At this moment there's no need to have that in court. If that's the result that that's their position, we'll hear that as well. Now we'll move on and could the witness be escorted -- oh, one second, please. One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there is one urgent matter I don't know if I have to address you, Mr. Weber or Mr. Tieger. On 25th of September the Defence filed a motion - and I think it's public - to hear David Del Pinto's evidence via video-conference link during the week of the 19th of October, 2015, or at another agreeable date. And considering that the Defence's preferred date of testimony is only a few weeks away, the Chamber invites the Prosecution to provide an expedited response.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And we will do exactly that, Mr. President. We're working on it now. It may involve a quick discussion with the Defence, but we'll keep that in mind and get back to the Court as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Earlier, when I addressed the urgent matter, I said on the 25th of September the Defence filed a motion and I said I think it's public. It's not a public motion. However, nothing was touched upon which caused the motion to be confidential; and for that reason there's no need for a redaction of the transcript, but I'll be more cautious next time. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you again that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Lukic will now continue his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I couldn't translate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could we check. Perhaps it's the volume; perhaps it's the channel. Can you hear me now? Can you hear me now in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No translate. Uh-huh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you receive translation now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it was the easiest probably to resolve today, I think. I remind you again that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, and Mr. Lukic will now continue his examination-in-chief. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you allow me to address you, Your Honours? I want to say something regarding yesterday's testimony before we begin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may do so briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very briefly. Yesterday after leaving the courtroom I realised, because the whole thing shocked me, rather, I confused the artefacts in court when I spoke about the object that was in the courtroom, the stabiliser from the Markale I incident. I was talking about events concerning the identification in this courtroom of the artefact from Markale II, so everything I said yesterday is related to the artefact that is only going to be shown later, Markale II, whereas, the artefact we had in the courtroom from Markale I, we saw in September 2012. And it was the representative of the Registry who brought it into our rooms. Mr. Poparic, Aleksandar Stefanovic, and I were in the room, and, of course, the person from the Registry. We reviewed on that occasion the documentation, we measured the length of the stabiliser. I apologise from -- for this error. It must have been caused by my great surprise over what I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Does that mean whatever you said about what happened and trying to unscrew, et cetera, and that you thought it would be of no use because you considered it to be impossible, that also now relates to when you inspected the Markale II artefact; is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for this correction. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need on our screens 1D05496, and that is an expert analysis relating to Markale. In English, we need page 97 because we need figure 95; and in B/C/S it would be page 143. As a reference, this photograph was taken from a video which is 65 ter 1D05915, and this still is taken from 0021 minutes and 49 seconds. We will also tender that video, or do you wish to see those couple of seconds from which the still was taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm asking if you want to see those couple of seconds or still is enough, because we just need the still?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do not ask for anything in addition to what you're presenting to us; and if that changes, we'll let you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Ms. Subotic, in this figure, 95, we see - as we see on the video - that this man who is sitting is injured. Below the photograph, the caption -- there is a legend, number 1 is the site of the explosion; number 2 is the injured man, who is conscious with his lower leg amputated; and 3 is injured man sitting. How far is the site distant from these people marked 1, 2, 3?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the documentation we found, which was prepared by a team from the CSB, the site of the explosion is 1.95 metres from the curb, no more than 2 metres, in my estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you just said those people marked 1, 2, 3. But 1 is not a marking of a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The people marked numbers 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: People marked as 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, you misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I also ask for clarification here. Point 1 on this picture is called "point of impact," and your question now, Mr. Lukic - as explained by the witnesses - relates to the site of the explosion. My question is: What is the difference between "site of explosion" and "point of impact"?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know how that was translated. I said -- [Interpretation] I said "place of the explosion." I didn't know how it was translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, in your question, I can quote you, you said: "How far is it the site distant from these people marked 1, 2, and 3?" I was going to interrupt you and ask you: Site of what? But then the witness carried on to answer, understood you to talk of the site of the explosion; in her answer, that's what she says. Because in her answer she says: "According to the documentation we found which was prepared by a team from the CSB the site of the explosion is ..." So I'm asking: What is the difference between the "site of explosion" and the "point of impact" that is referred to in the picture, which is here where these people are, not 1.5 metres away?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's translation issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think you expressed yourself also in B/C/S and you said that you said "mesto eksplozije," which is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "Point of impact" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- B -- well, "point of impact," but was translated a moment later as the "site of the" --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Explosion."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- "explosion." So if the parties would -- or Mr. Lukic, you used the language "mesto eksplozije." That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And you consider -- in your understanding of your own language, does that mean that the site of the explosion is the same as the point where the shell impacted?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's how I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how you understand it; for you, it's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For me, it's the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's move on. What, of course, remains is that it is in the written version, it is translated as "point of impact"; and in our oral interpretation, it was interpreted as the "site of the impact." Now I think the question is whether it's the same or not. It's certainly not the same words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's certainly not the same words. Let me explain my problem. My problem is: According to the witness, the site of explosion is some 1.5 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think 195.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 1.95, yeah. My question is: Away from what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From the curb, I think she said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: From the curb?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And how does it relate -- how far is it from this 1.1 or is this 1.1 said to be 1.95 metres away?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Then I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Having resolved all the misunderstandings, please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have figure 96, please, it's same page in English; and the next page, 144, in B/C/S. This is just the same -- probably the same moment from another angle, only this one is recorded in 65 ter video number 1D01227A at 0 hours, 01 minute, and 34 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have the English version on our screen as well. I think I'm looking at --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, the first line on this page is the second line of the text underneath the picture --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, okay, then we have to go back --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- that figure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and we have to go back one page in English, so as to be able to read the -- yes. Figures 96 reading: "Men who survived explosion of a 120-millimetre mortar shell 2 metres away." Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We referenced video from which this picture is taken. Now we'll have -- we could -- we should go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Don't you put a question to the witness with respect to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, is it the same place from a different angle or are these two different places? And in which one do you better see the point of impact?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same place photographed from another side. And in the previous photograph, I would say the point of impact is seen more clearly and it gives one a better picture of that space. In any case, in figure 96, this man whom we see is the same man as marked number 2 in the previous picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the one lying down or the one sitting?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one who is half-sitting, trying to find some help; the one with a amputated leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you draw any conclusions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the person sitting in this picture or a person sitting in another picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, both lying but both lifted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic, if you want us to hear any conclusions to be drawn on the previous picture we had one as the "mesto eksplozije" - I don't use the English language any further - and we had two persons. Okay, now first, are we now talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Number 2, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Number 2. And that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- a man who is lying down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that's a man who is lying down and not a man who is sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we go back to the previous so that we can well memorize -- yes. Number 2 is not a sitting person. It is a person you say is lying and he is not the one with the amputated leg, or is he?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now do we see that here because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- not from this angle we cannot see his legs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we cannot see his legs --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- but we can see that he is a bit lifted as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He -- well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: His head is not on the pavement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- well, you're giving evidence at this moment. We can see what we see, and later you argue that he's not lying for the full hundred per cent but is a little bit upright. And do I see that that is a person not with a white or whitish shirt -- as a matter of fact, I can't see -- it's dark. That's what it is, what we can see, nothing more, nothing less. Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could the witness perhaps mark the person she was talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps that would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Figure 96.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, is this person you marked with the circle the same person as number 2 in figure 95?

utterances.text: And when you marked the person in figure 96, what -- I'm now a little bit confused because are you not certain about the person you marked or what is your position? Can you help us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The person I marked is about 1 metre from the point of impact. And as far as I can see in the film, his legs are amputated, he is trying to lift himself up, and looking for help. If you look at the video and all these scenes in sequence, it will be much clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I'm asking about --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It could be the person marked 2 in figure 95 because he is approximately in the same place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But I take it you are not certain about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, one cannot be quite sure, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now, you said both legs were amputated. I understood from your previous answers that a leg was - that means one leg - was amputated. What is it in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my opinion, as far as I can see - but I cannot be sure - it looks like both legs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I have a few follow-up questions there as well. Mr. Lukic -- no. First of all, trying to get a bit upright, does that mean that you consider these two photographs to have been taken at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, not in the very same moment were these pictures made from two different directions, because obviously in figure 96 some of the people are missing because they had already been taken away, injured people. Some of them had been taken away, although the interval is very small. If you look at the road, some of the injured people are already missing, whereas we can see seem this figure 95. But, still, a lot of the injured people are still there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it's a picture taken at not the same moment, where you're not sure whether the person number 2 in picture 95 is the same as the one you marked on 96. Do you have any clue as to how much time there was between the two pictures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but a very short time, I suppose, because the evacuation proceeded very fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's not something which is in the realm of your expertise, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thought to avoid showing the video, but let's have 1D5915 from [indiscernible] 21 minutes, 42 seconds to 21 minutes 49 seconds --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we had a marked picture. Now the marking is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, we can -- gone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it still retrievable? I take it that you want the marked -- and do we have them -- you tender that, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The marked figure 96 of the document 1D5496 receives Exhibit Number D1264, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We'll first --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Would that be the full screen with the figure 95 also in it, or just the marked figure of 96?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's only the marked figure 96, but since the other one is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's everything, so it's even easier to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to compare the two pictures. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm -- just spoke with Mr. Ivetic. He told me that he has another video on his screen and then we'll move to the previous one. So we'll see first 1D01227A from 1 minute, 32 seconds to 1 minute, 34 seconds. Can we start.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we go back, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that on this video we see that both legs were amputated, but that's my opinion.

And that the Chamber will finally determine whether it sees anything here relevant and what that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution's position would be - and we've had witnesses comment on the images from our colleague too - that the Chamber, I understand, would evaluate that and it's in the totality of the evidence that it has before us. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same position here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same position, that's good. Please proceed.

utterances.text: So we just wanted to show it and we would offer both videos into evidence as well.

utterances.text: And you are not relying on the text spoken?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we just need the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER

utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean, this is -- the proponent into evidence is the Defence. The Defence is seeking to admit it. If they want the Chamber to consider it, then --

utterances.text: To consider the --

utterances.text: -- the video, where it's from, its context, we would like to have the -- I mean, they're offering it into evidence. I don't see what's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the Defence is tendering this video, asking the Chamber to pay attention only to the images, whereas the Defence claims - I don't know on what basis exactly - but that this is a video taken immediately after the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, you just pointed out the reason we'd like the -- it transcribed, so we understand what is being depicted and what is being broadcast and shown.
