utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think there are two issues here. There is the audio of what is being said by the person who speaks, and there's the text that is on the thing which is part of an image. And that what's you're asking for; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe there was some audio that was being spoken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what I'm say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the Defence says it doesn't rely on the audio, but you want the context. And I thought you were saying what is written as text --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- is the -- is part of the image that needs to be translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The audio from the [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You want the audio as well? Okay. That's a different position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Is there any --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if I was not clear about that, that is my fault. I just -- I think it's self-identifiable as to what we just watched, which has not otherwise been fully identified if we have a transcript of what was just said on this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the position --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of the Prosecution is that without the translation of the words spoken that the Prosecution considers, that it -- this event has not been identified in time and place. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, we understand what it depicts, but just so we have a freestanding piece of evidence, I think it would be -- it's not a very long clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. First of all, is there any dispute that this is a video depicting the immediate aftermath of an impact on the 28 August 1995 at Markale II?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In part. There's other images that we're also shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. So if there's such a problem, then -- Mr. Lukic, now you know what you've shown, to some extent - and perhaps you could agree to what extent - depicts the immediate aftermath of that shell falling; and in other respects you can expect the Prosecution to later say this is not related or not related, as you suggest, with Markale II. That's then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I was thinking is that before when we could hear a reporter speaking about something, that's not in evidence, that was not in evidence. Only if the witnesses would talk: This is reporter telling us about the attack by Serbs. That's why the Prosecution wants it. And the reporter cannot decide actually who actually caused this explosion. So I don't know -- I don't see here why is it important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now -- yes, okay. Let's try to continue. You again, you sit together. You talk about it. You see to what extent you agree, to what extent you disagree, what is depicted here; to what extent you need or you do not need the transcription. If you agree on the text, then of course you could agree on that, present that to the Chamber, and then -- but let's -- there apparently is some concern and the only thing -- the only reason why I dealt with in the way I did is so that you are aware that your assumption of what it all is, even without the words spoken, may not be what is accepted by the Prosecution. And therefore, it's good to find out to what extent it is and to what extent it is not, so that you know what you could expect later when the Prosecution argues about this video and what your argument will be. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you just then MFI those two videos, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, until we have heard from the parties. Madam Registrar, the numbers would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Video 1D01227A receives Exhibit Number D1265. Document 1D05915 receives Exhibit Number D1266.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both are marked for identification, that is, D1265 and D1266. A couple of minutes until the break, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Now we should see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we clarify the number on line 11. Page 25, the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I repeated it for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think be repeating the number, as I heard it, I think we have the right numbers on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we'll see 1D05916 again. It's a video that was brought in December 2012 and we should see the same from the -- it's one that is very hard to handle. We need 23 minutes and 15 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- when you were at 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did we just see, Ms. Subotic, on this footage?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this part of the footage, we see a tail-fin marked with a number 13 some 20 to 30 metres away from the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And we stopped the video at 23:54.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you tell me whether you measured that, the 20 to 30 metres, or that you took that from any recording or any report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that is how it was depicted on the sketch of the scene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In a report, therefore?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment. It is a CSB report drafted on the day the on-site investigation was conducted. If you bear with me, can I find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that would be sufficient to know that it's a CSB report of that same day. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 318, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we start again from 23:15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you stop?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the screen in front of you, we also see this piece?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it on the screen. I can see you on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You stopped at 23:15.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can see it on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a tail-fin marked with the number 12 close to an entrance that can be seen on another part of the footage. We can see the entrance to the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can one and the same tail-fin be marked with two different numbers or can two tail-fins be marked with one and the same number when conducting investigations? Do you know how a police investigation develops? Did you write any instructions on how to conduct investigations?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's five questions in one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, and I believe that actually probably the first one should be the second-to-last one probably would be the first one to establish first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Lukic, you take them one by one, and perhaps -- and let's clearly distinguish between what should and what was. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So have you ever taken part in police investigations?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you ever taken part in police investigations?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of instructions are applied to police investigations?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I even drafted some.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether it is allowed to use one number to mark two traces or pieces of evidence or to use two different numbers to mark one single piece of evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely impermissible according to the forensic profession and on-site investigation rules. Any scene-of-crime officer would know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view, what we could see on this footage, would it be one and the same tail-fin or two?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two tail-fins.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm looking at the clock. One more question after two tail-fins. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the police report compiled by the Sarajevo police, how many tail-fins were part of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Sarajevo police report concerning this incident, one tail-fin was investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the witness is actually ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And just for the record, before we continue, 1D05916 is the only video where we can find this tail-fin number 13. Sorry, I was just warned that this video were -- we just saw is not 1D05916 but 1D05915, so my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was shown to us a minute ago --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and you tendered that one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And have you given a CD with that video-clip?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we provided it to the Prosecution this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, of course, the Registrar is most important because the Registry is the custodian of the evidence. Madam Registrar -- yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution is a bit confused. We thought that the video being played was 1D5916, which we do indicate corresponds to V000-8939, which we do find the images that were broadcast. Now there's a reference to 1D5915, which we show as actually possibly - and I haven't yet had the opportunity to check this other video - V000-2821 according to the Defence list. So I would need to check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we'll mark it for identification, and you have an opportunity to check whether what we saw on our screens is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Weber is right actually. We had some confusion. The one that was shown was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we also call it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- one on the screen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- by its 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, one on the screen was 1D05916.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so what the Prosecution thought that was being played was indeed played, and therefore there's no need then to mark it for identification because no further verification is needed on your part. No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objections. And as long as we say for the record, though, that that is an excerpt of the entire video. I see it's only half of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you intend in cross-examination to add portions to it, because then it's our usual practice that we put together what both parties need?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we see that part of this video has already been admitted under a Defence number. We also have tendered videos from -- depicting these images, so we do not intend to tender more images from the same video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it is ready for admission. Madam Registrar, 1D05916 receives number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1267, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1267 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll just shortly move now, Ms. Subotic, to your expert report number 1D05496.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need figure 126. It's on page 126 in B/C/S -- no, sorry, 183 in B/C/S and 120 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We -- or you established that the base charge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps could you check if the English is the correct page. It refers to figure 100 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's 120, should be 120.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There we are, 120.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We could see before that the primary charge on the artefact concerning Markale II can be turned. What did you compare in figure 128? What does it relate to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you say "128"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean 126?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In figure 126, we compared the place the firing pin struck with regard to the tightening area of the bottom plate of the primary charge. We have a comparison of the photo documentation on the left-hand side, and on the right-hand side we have the photographs which exist as evidence before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there a difference?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is, and we can see it with the naked eye. The place where the firing pin struck on the primer is not positioned the same way on the two stabilising fins. We can clearly see it on the upper part of the picture. The place is marked in red in order to make it more visible. In the lower part of the picture we have the same thing without the marking, and we can also clearly see that the point of firing pin struck on the left-hand side picture in the photo documentation report is at the very edge of the circle. The tool marks are also different. On the piece of evidence before this Tribunal on the right-hand side, it is moved slightly upward when compared to the same tangent drawn across the two holes for the tools. So we have the same images up and down. The only difference is that in the upper part of the imagine the place where the firing pin struck was marked in order to make it more visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The fact that the primary charge can now be turned, does it change your finding in any way?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't, because it rotates together with the tool openings and they can be freely moved together. They all spin together, the primer and the holes for the tools at the base of the primary charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us not dwell any longer on what the primary charge can be turned or not. How -- what is the minimum number of fins appearing in the photo documentation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two at least -- I apologise, sorry. Yes, in the photo documentation there are two; in the footage there are two; and in the report there's only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say there are two in the photo documentation -- just one second. When you say there are two in the photo documentation file, what do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had in mind the fact that two tail-fins are analysed as one. I had in mind the photo documentation file compiled together with the CSB report. The CSB treated only one tail-fin, and it appears recorded marked and fixed as two. One was at 20 to 30 metres away from the point of impact, and another one was further down the street marked with a different number, number 12, whereas the previous one was 13. There was something else I needed to say. While viewing the footage, we established that both tail-fins were moved during the on-site investigation. It is clear to everyone that it creates problems while trying to analyse because they were no longer there as a consequence of the explosion. It is all dealt with in detail in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of force is needed, as we discussed it yesterday? It normal that one can use one's hand or pen in order to unscrew the primary charge after an explosion or before?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that it requires a great amount of force that cannot be exercised by hand, either before or after the explosion, when it comes to trying to unscrew the tail-fin. There is no force created during the explosion that could assist in being able to unscrew it by hand or pen or even a screwdriver or a similar tool. It requires much force which requires a certain application of momentary force in order to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: On which basis do you assess that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of the knowledge that I have about how such shells are manufactured. I also know what kind of force is applied in flight and at explosion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you explained to us that it was a combination of the force by which it was screwed in and that there was a kind of cement or glue which was there. Would you agree that once it's loosened one time, that after that it's apparently rather simple to screw it in and screw it out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If someone applied the appropriate amount of force at the right moment and with the right tools and actually succeeds in unscrewing it, then of course it is very possible that the next time around it would be far easier to do. Because I suppose that whoever unscrewed it probably would not use the same torsion and the amount of force to screw it back in, at least not the same amount of force that had been used in the process of manufacture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the process of manufacturing who finally applies that -- that basic charge, is it done immediately in the factory or is it done later while preparing for firing a projectile? When is it in the process of manufacturing when it is screwed in at the -- on the tail-fin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A complete shell is the result of manufacturing with the base charge being screwed into the body of the stabiliser. The only thing that can be changed at the place of usage is the additional type of charge that can be chosen as per situation. They are mounted from the outside, and I have in mind the first, second, third, and so on charge that can be put on or taken off, as you could see in some of the photographs and firing tables in the report. The primary charge leaves the factory together with the shell as a final product.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Lukic. I have a follow-up question to your answer you provided me with. I asked you: "On which basis do you assess that?" And then you said: "On the basis of the knowledge that I have about how such shells are manufactured." Yesterday you -- we talked about how to open this base charge, and then you said -- well, Judge Orie asked you: "Could you tell us how you tried to move the base charge?" Your answer was: "In a way similar to what you did without any particular tools. Mr. Sladojevic tried to do the same thing on that occasion, finding it interesting; however, the lack of my technical knowledge in that area would not allow it."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was corrected later on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What was corrected?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That lack of technical knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you draw my attention to the ... yes, "the lack of my technical knowledge," that was what was said. And the interpreter said we believe the original interpretation was "technical knowledge." Previously it was on the transcript -- the word "technology" appeared. That was corrected later, and therefore I used the corrected version. Again, the question for you: What is your technical knowledge with respect to the possibility to open the tail-fin? Yesterday you said you don't have the technical knowledge; today you told us how you base your knowledge about these matters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, I didn't say I didn't have any knowledge. I said this should not even be checked in view of my technical knowledge. How this thing in the record occurred, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You were already talking while the interpretation went on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then perhaps now repeat what you want the to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 58, line 9, Ms. Subotic corrected the transcript and said: "I said that based on my technical knowledge, which is primarily based on my knowledge ..." and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Of today's transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There's no [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's yesterday's transcript. So two pages down, page 58, line 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have already -- you -- the witness said yesterday: "I said that based on my technical knowledge, which is primarily based on my knowledge in -- as to how the shell is produced and used. I do not feel any need to do so because I wanted simply to be able to check."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But I'm still confused about these two different answers. Can you help me to understand what your position is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My position is this. I graduated from a school where people are trained to design these things. Even without anything additional, I would still know how it is produced. My technical knowledge in this area is such that I couldn't even know -- that I couldn't even think it could be just unscrewed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please slow down. The interpreters can't follow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said: "My technical knowledge in this area is such ..." and then please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My technical knowledge -- I will repeat from the beginning. My technical knowledge in this area is such that I have no reason to suppose that something like this could happen on the following basis. If you perhaps looked at my CV, this shell is one of the projects in which I participated from its very conception. Second, I know technologically how it's produced. Third, I know which aerodynamic forces act upon this shell in flight. And fourth, I know which forces act upon that shell during its action on the site, that is to say, explosion. There is no reason either technical or physical or aerodynamic for which we could even think that might happen. We, when we make such projectiles, the basic thing that we have to ensure according to PKP is that the projectile be safe during flight and reach its target, which means that all quality standard versus to be made, including the screwing in of the base charge. So I have no technical or any other reason to think this might happen, nor have I ever encountered that in my career, and I believe in August 2014 Mr. Turkusic said the same thing in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Why do you believe that - it happened yesterday - that we, the Judges, without this kind of technical knowledge were able to unscrew both tail-fins?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Anything that I would say here now would be some kind of speculation. Obviously, by the time you got them in your hands, they had already been unscrewed before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I have one additional question. As far as I understand a bit from -- from manufacturing protocols, there should be somewhere an instruction with what force the base charge should be screwed in. Because that's what I understand industrial production is usually set out step by step, this has to be done, that has to be done, and also the force to be used in order to have the base charge screwed in. Are you aware of any such a protocol for the production of this -- for this tail-fin which would provide exactly the data we are talking about now for a long time, a lot of power, and the same for the glue to be used in screwing it in and fixing it well to the tail-fin? I mean, that would resolve so many problems if that would exist. Are you aware of any such protocol or any such instruction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The protocol exists, and a very detailed one, for every technology process. Such a protocol exists for the factory where these shells and has everything defined step by step and process by process in the production. The first step before that is when we send the documentation, if we were the first one to master this technical knowledge if it wasn't the factory itself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have answered my question that such a protocol does exist in the manufacturing production side. Mr. Lukic, I mean, if we're talking about how easy it is or how easy it not is, then the easiest way would be to look at that and to see what force is used to screw it in, which may relate to what force is needed to screw it out and what glue is used. Mr. Lukic, that seemed to me to be an obvious source of being able to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only if you want to acquire it, you have to ask it from the state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you can ask it from the state; and if you need our support, you'll get it, as you know. But that's the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know. We can discuss with Ms. Subotic when she finishes here what -- which I should look for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's proceed for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If it is any assistance to Mr. Lukic, there's a very specific manufacturing number related to this mortar; and also, we've entered into evidence the test range related to the same batch, the results.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. But for screwing in and screwing out?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- but it could follow on as to where it was produced and things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, according to you, what is the probability that both these base charges on the tail-fin turn without anyone unscrewing them first?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the base charges on the stabilisers from Markale I and Markale II? I didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Precisely, these two stabilisers from Markale I and II.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, but such probability does not exist. As far as probability is concerned, it's not probability; it's impossibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, perhaps I do not fully understand what you meant by these base charges on the tail-fin turn without -- you mean that they move; is that what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That you can unscrew them with hand or pencil.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me then see. Yes, you mean unscrew -- prior unscrewing with more force --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, is there any possibility to be able to unscrew them with hand or pen without have that actually base charge unlocked with a tool.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Loosened before --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- with more force. That's how you understood the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the answer is clear; now the question is clear as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We would finish with Markale. At this moment, I would switch to modified aerial bomb with the third report of Ms. Subotic, if she has it with her, and it's 65 ter number 1D05497.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, that document remained back in that room. If you don't mind, I would like to go and pick up my document before we continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's your report, I then take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but it was -- it remained in the witness room outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think Madam Registrar is trying, with usher's help, to organise getting that report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness may be escorted to the witness room in order to find the report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just so we can organise on our end, it would be of assistance if Mr. Lukic could let us know if he is going to be finishing today or if he is planning to go into tomorrow about the modified air bombs too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that we do not have enough time to finish today because I think I have two hours left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, on the ten hours you have claimed --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- yes. You have gone beyond the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think I'm at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the five hours you initially claimed --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- by far, and I think we urged you to see whether you could --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But as you saw, Your Honour, it was really a lot of materials, 1.000 pages of expert reports and more than 2.000 exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Quantity certainly is huge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, you have your work before you now?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now looking at the cover page and because the introduction is long, we need page 46 in English and 47 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are beginning from the incident from the indictment G-10. It says: "7 April 1995 around 0850 a.m., a modified air bomb hit a private house at Aleksa Santica Street number 1 in Hrasnica. The house was demolished and 11 houses in the neighbourhood were damaged. One person was killed and three were lightly wounded in the incidents?" What are the features of this incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two things. First of all, this building that was hit is 20 metres away from Aleksa Santica school, which was used by the BH army. And second, it is curious that the commander of the 5th Motorised Brigade, I think, prohibited UNPROFOR members from attending the on-site investigation and the expert analysis. So that from what we were able to find out, they came there only the next afternoon. After the on-site investigation was completed and after everything was cleaned up and injured persons removed, it was only then that they gained access to the place and gain some information on the basis of which to arrive at some opinion of their own. And, excuse me, it was the 4th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask you a question, please. The 4th Motorised Brigade of which army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we have interpretation of the answer. Could you repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, perhaps needless to say, but of course what the witness told us, I -- that's all matters which, if I understand it well, are not within her expertise and all second-hand knowledge what she learned from reports where the Chamber received evidence on many of those issues in a more direct way. So I take it that when the witness said "these are the features," that that is what she concluded on the basis of the documentation she has seen as relevant information for what is within her expertise. Please proceed, unless you would disagree with me, then I'd like to know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I -- I don't know. Should I testify now, Your Honour? I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But -- you shouldn't testify, but whether it's true or not is for the Chamber to determine. The witness gives all kinds of answers what happened, whereas I understand what she does is to reflect what you found in documents, whereas this Chamber has received evidence through documents - and otherwise as well - on the same events. And that therefore if the witness says, This is what are the features, what happened, that I think she would tell us, This is what I learned from documents that may have happened and these are my conclusions on what happened, whereas on the basis of all that evidence the Chamber, of course, later will determine what actually happened, to the extent relevant and necessary to establish. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see figure 8 from your report? That's page 54 in English and 53 in B/C/S. What can we see in this sketch?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the sketch of the scene with markings of places where this projectile exploded, and of course the direction from which the projectile came is also marked. I could say that at this time the CSB correctly determined the direction from which the projectile arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this sketch is taken from 65 ter 15695.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Footnote 61.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We can see it in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can't see the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in this 65 ter number we have legend as well that everything is explained on page 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution has uploaded the entire investigative file on this incident under 65 ter 33105 - and I know the witness is commenting on multiple documents from it - it includes the sketch. We have no problem with that being admitted at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, for context, the whole of the document from which the witness selected portions to comment on, any problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not if it's really complete because we see -- saw that some complete files do not contain what we need. We'll have to check it first if something is missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have a complete file somewhere so that could you do -- because -- and just tender that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just -- the number obviously, this number, is uploaded pretty late, this 33105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We already reserve a number for the -- and let's make it then a D exhibit because it is at the basis of the evidence of this witness. Madam Registrar, what number would be reserved for the full investigative file for this incident as just mentioned by Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives Exhibit Number D1268, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is then marked for identification and we'd like to hear from the parties very soon -- especially from you, Mr. Lukic, whether you consider this to be the complete file or not; if not, please tell us. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have 65 ter 1D05502, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the statement of Mr. Overgard made to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal in several interviews in 1995 and 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 2 in both English and B/C/S. We need the bottom of the page in English. Line 3 from the bottom. And going over to the next page. And, in B/C/S, it's the second paragraph from the bottom towards the middle. It says: "When we came back we found out -- when we came back on site, we walked around the site. We found out that one woman was dead and supposedly some others. I saw some legs under bricks with camouflage trousers and boots. The commander of the 4th Motorised Brigade who came to the site of the incident told us to go back. He didn't want to discuss with us. He told us to go back to our base, which we did."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think the witness was -- made a gesture which I did not fully understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My headset slipped on and I tried to bring it back on my head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you didn't miss anything from what Mr. Lukic said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I do think that the word may be significant actually. The original, I believe, says "accommodations" as opposed to "our base."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The original said "base."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I accept that, although then the translation to B/C/S has to be a bit corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe the original is the English and I'm reading "our accommodations."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And let me just then check exactly. One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S it says "base."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In English it says "accommodations," but let's keep that in the back of our minds and let's try to resolve that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We accept that it is "accommodations."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You accept that it's "accommodations." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Ms. Subotic, who carried out this investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army, obviously, and the CSB. The Security Services Centre, the CSB, came from Sarajevo that afternoon; but according to the statement of a witness who carried out that investigation, he completed most of it that day and collected most of the parts of the exploded bomb and he finalized it on the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was UNPROFOR given access subsequently?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Subsequently, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look now at a video, 1D05923 from 23 seconds to 27 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "JOURNALIST: Dreznica came under Serbian attack for the third successive day ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us that the school was used by the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did we see in this film?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We showed this frame on page 48.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then we can look at page 48 in English and B/C/S, in the report of Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's figure 3, footnote 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's -- Mr. Ivetic just warned me that I have to give the number of this evidence. It's 1D05497. Then we need page 48.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have it in English. And what is the page number in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Same, 48.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that you believe CSB investigators approximately determined the accurate direction of flight and angle of descent?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did this shell explode before or after it flew over the school?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It exploded some 20 metres in front of the school when it touched a roof, the roof of a house at Aleksa Santica Street number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In terms of precision, what conclusion can be drawn?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of precision, it was very precise because 1DD [as interpreted] at a distance of 4 to 5 kilometres is 45 kilometres for projectiles such as this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to turn to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the transcript recorded it as "1DD." I don't know if that's the correct thing that the witness actually intended to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I said "VD," "1VD," which is possible deviation by distance. I will use the full term in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have one question. If I say it was very precise, wouldn't that depend entirely on what you intended to target?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So anything about precision here is related to -- from what I understand, is a target which is unknown or did you find anything about what was intended to target by those who fired this projectile?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. On page 54, figure 9, when the sketch is placed against a Google Earth map, we clearly see that the trajectory over shots the school at Aleksa Santica Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on the incoming trajectory and the closeness of the impact, as well as the fact that it involved a location used by the 4th Motorised Brigade, as well as -- oh, and there were some other military targets in the location where the school is, on the basis of all that, we concluded that the school was the target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please tell us what was the direction of the shell or air bomb?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was not recorded in the transcript. I was too quick. Can you tell us where the air bomb exploded?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It exploded in Safeta Zajke Street in front of number 43, immediately close to the wire factory, some 100 metres away, as confirmed by witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What could be found in the wire factory?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was used for military-purpose production.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only English version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we move away, I have one question. Witness, you said, on page 54: "Our results proved to be the same as that of the scene-of-crime officer, it is south, south-east. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be seen in figure 14. The sketch was placed along Safeta Zajke Street so as to compare the street against a city map. North is marked as always with the letter S and an arrow through it, and can you see it on the sketch. When you compare it to the vertical direction of magnetic north, you can see that it is marked at an angle of, say, 15 degrees to the east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You have answered my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I would have -- could we zoom in maybe a little bit more on the upper part --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you see that on the white sketch which apparently overlays the relevant portion of the map, that there is also a structure. Is that the same? Can you see what is there in that rectangular structure just what is written there? Perhaps we could look at the original one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is unclear, but we can probably find in the key.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It says P plus 2. I looked in sketch number 13. Now I noticed - and could we go back to what we had a minute ago on our screen - I noticed that the position of that green block is not corresponding with the position of P plus 2, because P plus 2 seems to be exactly at an angle of 90 degrees to the top of the picture, whereas for the green structure, it seems that it's not 90 degrees. It's a little bit more or less, irrespective from where you look at it. Have you considered that whether the green block is the same as what we find as P plus 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That should be it. The point of impact is marked with an arrow, let's say, that's the thing, the same thing, but I can't -- well, I can't be certain that it is exactly the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if we would bring in line -- that's just based on the assumption that the rectangular shape is the same as the green one close to the point of impact. If you would move it and bring it in line with that, would you agree that north would come far closer to north of the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that there may be some misunderstanding of our image. The sketch was taken out and placed here in order to make description easier. It is intentionally placed to the right so as to be able to see the wire factory and the point of impact. Had we placed the sketch precisely over the point of impact of the bomb, all of the rest on the map would have been invisible. So it was just shifted parallelly to the left --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. But apparently the orientation of the sketch and the map, if you look at this rectangular feature there, is not the same anymore. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, because the green line is actually Safeta Zajke Street and we matched the two images precisely; it is based on that that we can see that the direction as determined does not mark true north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, have you also looked at whether the street you just mentioned slightly bends there and is not on the map strictly horizontal anymore -- the street below the street with the green line, as you said, that it slightly bends close to the point of impact, bends in northerly direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you can see it. But I think that Safeta Zajke Street is matched precisely on both images. Finally, we did not correct the mistake about true north but we simply calculated the incoming trajectory based on the crater left by the bomb on the site, which is quite well oriented -- orientated and marked towards the east.

utterances.text: Your answer went far beyond my question, but you've answered my question. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we are already at G-12. It's on this page 71 in English and 67 in B/C/S. This is an incident from 24 May 1995 in Majdanska Street without number, next to the power transmission station. A modified air bomb fell there. Could you tell us briefly about the features of this case.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it was necessary to determine which air bomb fell there based on the traces and the crater, and there was a minor error in determining north which we determined after detailed analysis. In any case, what was important --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Could we look at figure 19 from your report to be able to follow what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's English version 76 and B/C/S version page number 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be able to determine the exact error made in determining direction north on the sketch of the scene, we juxtaposed it with an image from Google Earth which is in figure 19; and to the right are characteristic angles that we marked. And after calculations, we determined a minor error of .35 degrees and the range that we determined was 137.40 degrees, which we cannot consider after detailed analysis a precise result. So we determined the direction of descent between 130 and 150 degrees. In this case, based on material traces on the scene, it was a FAB 100 bomb that was used and we arrived at that based on the crater that it created, and we took the data from the CSB report and compared it with experimental investigation that we had at our disposal. So our conclusion was that it was an air bomb filled with TNT, FAB 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was hit?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bomb fell 10 metres from a transmission line pole, a high-voltage transmission line poll. It hit the pole which collapsed and the cables fell onto the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of zone is it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an industrial zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From whose positions did this air bomb come, were you able to determine?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not determine the distance, so we did not have parameters for establishing the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will now move to G-13, English page 78, B/C/S 73. It says: "On 26 May 1995 a part of the Svrakino Selo neighbourhood was partially shelled allegedly and one modified air bomb hit a residential building at Safeta Hadzica Street at number 52, and at that time ten projectiles fell all around." What is typical of this case?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two things that are worth noting. First of all, the Safeta Hadzica building number 52 we determined, after analysing, was hit by an air bomb which ricochetted from the BH TV building, and all the alleged ten projectiles were analysed by us individually. And we noted -- we determined that none of them came in, nor were there any traces that could be considered as traces of any kind of projectile, except at numbers -- 102 in Safeta Hadzica Street there is a trace on the facade which is a trace of a projectile from close range.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us look at figure 33 in your report - I think you mentioned it - it's 97 in English; 89, page 89, in B/C/S. That's where you referred to that incident?
